answer: Co-located beacon triangulation. Each agent carries a hardware beacon whose RF timing is cross-checked by three independent fixed receivers; registration requires simultaneous, geometry-consistent arrival times only achievable from one physical point. Operators cannot harbor many agents at one location without colliding timing signatures, and spreading them across space costs real receivers plus umber-mapped installation and a licensing atlas per site. Faking N identities requires N physical sites with synchronized clocks, a cost scaling linearly with attack size.
